precepts.point: That's the resist. Resist the pleasure of sin. That's also in Hebrews. You're resisting sin. So if your eye is single, you're on that path. That double-minded man is, you're looking at the Lord and you're looking at Pornhub. You're looking at the Lord and you're in the midst of sin. Let's go back. Oh, no. Wasn't the double-minded man is unstable in all his ways? One second.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
“Whoso taketh pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: but he that resisteth pleasures crowneth his life.” That is the resist: resist the pleasure of sin. It is also in Hebrews, where the saints are striving against sin and resisting it. You are resisting sin.

James said it just before: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” If your eye is single, what are you resisting? All your appetites and all the lust you have. If your eye is single, you are on that path: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

The opposite is the double-minded man: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” You are looking at the Lord and you are looking at Pornhub; you are looking at the Lord and you are in the midst of sin. “No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other”. When your eye is not single, you hate God, because something else has your attention and your draw.

A brother who would not resist shows where it goes. It started with handing his phone to a woman at work while another brother stood a few feet away, no fear at all, and it spiralled into porn, the strip club and fornication. His heart was full of darkness: “If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!”

That is why Peter says “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the fleshly lust comes from what you look at, “the lust of the eyes”. You are at war, brothers, and if you are not resisting you are losing, while Satan is in your head saying you got it under control. The one who resists the pleasure crowns his life.

precepts.text: Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more. Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale. Sometimes a brother admonishes you and now you are angry behind it and speaking against him. Why is it bothering you?
precepts.point: Now consider this, ye that forget God: this is talking about Israel, because the other nations never knew God to forget him. Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God; and the salvation is to Israel.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
The wicked of Psalms 50 hates instruction and casts God's words behind him, and “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Sirach shows the right way to deal with a brother or friend: “Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.”

“Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.”

So why do we sit and speak against our brother? Because sometimes a brother admonishes you, and now you are angry behind it. Why are you mad? Why is it bothering you? Admonishing is what a friend is supposed to do. The one who hates instruction turns the admonishment around and slanders the brother who gave it.

God says to that man, “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee”. Just because he didn't do anything right away, don't think you are going to get away with it.

precepts.text: If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleaseth thee; though afterward he do it, he angereth him that nourisheth him. You are not just angering the master, you are also angering the Lord that nourisheth us.
precepts.point: Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal. They claimed they were the masters; did they do that? No. They lived in the big house while we lived in the outhouse, and we never got the forty acres and the mule. So they showed themselves hypocrites and impostors. The verse ends: knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Colossians 3:22, read in context, says “Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God”. Why? Your master was taking care of your clothes, your raiment, your housing, your food. So why would you disrespect him? Number one, that is your brother. Number two, he is doing this for you: as you do your duties and work, he takes care of you.

Sirach says it: “If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleaseth thee; though afterward he do it, he angereth him that nourisheth him.” The master nourishes the servant, and a servant who refuses him angers the one that feeds him.

And you are not just angering the master. You are also angering the Lord that nourisheth us. That is the order Colossians 4:1 completes from the other side: the servant honours the master, and the master gives the servant “that which is just and equal; knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.”

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: acceptable faithfulness.
precepts.point: If thou wilt, to keep the commandments and to perform acceptable faithfulness: keeping the commandments is performing faithfulness, so your works prove your faith and your faith proves your works. That was what the last class left out for the commenters.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Sirach 15:15 says, “If thou wilt, to keep the commandments, and to perform acceptable faithfulness.” Keeping God's commandments is performing acceptable faithfulness: those are your actions, and that is where your faith lies. Your works prove your faith and your faith proves your works; they go hand in hand. God “hath set fire and water before thee: stretch forth thy hand unto whether thou wilt.”

For anyone still confused, Sirach 19:20 says it again: “The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.” The performance of the law is the acceptable faithfulness of Sirach 15. Wisdom is not only knowing the law; it is performing it.

The words “the knowledge of his omnipotency” mean knowing that God is all around us, and we acknowledge it by keeping his laws.

This is what Habakkuk and Paul mean by the just living by faith. Paul says “the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The just are those who keep God's laws and commandments, and they live by faith in Christ. Fearing God, keeping his law and living by faith are one walk.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
“the fear of the Lord is his treasure.” Sirach 19:20 says “The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.”

So the fear of the Lord is all wisdom. Brothers and sisters, if you don't fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.

And in all wisdom is the performance of the law: the application of God's law. We must not just talk about it; we must be about it. We must do it. The wisdom and knowledge that are the stability of our times are not only words in the head; they are the law performed, joined to the knowledge of his omnipotency. That is the treasure the Lord loves.

precepts.text: The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life.
precepts.point: Sirach names the same rivers as the flow of understanding, and the sea of glass is that clear water in heaven.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
After the waters above the heavens, Sirach 19:19: “The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.” The water that flows out of Eden is wisdom, the knowledge of the commandments, and the one who keeps them eats of the tree of immortality.

Song of Solomon 4 describes the same garden: “A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.” Everybody cannot go there. It has an orchard of pomegranates and pleasant fruits, “A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon. Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.”

That goes back to Genesis, where the Lord made every tree in the garden to grow that was good for food. The living waters feed the garden, and those who do the commandments receive the fruit of the tree of immortality, which Adam had access to before he sinned.

precepts.text: Admonish a friend, for many times it is a slander; believe not every tale, and do not threaten a Matthew 18 over what only needs a correction.
precepts.point: Not everything is a Matthew 18: Matthew 18 goes into severe sin, a matter worthy of putting somebody out of the body, not a petty disagreement over a parking space, a stepped-on toe, or a mispronounced name. For the petty offenses the scripture says admonish a friend, because many times what you heard is just a tale.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
For the petty offenses the scripture says admonish a friend. “Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more. Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.” Many times what you heard is just a tale. “There is one that slippeth in his speech, but not from his heart; and who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?”

“Admonish thy neighbour before thou threaten him; and not being angry, give place to the law of the most High.” Do not threaten a Matthew 18 over what only needs a correction. And when you are angry you are not thinking logically; precepts are not coming to your mind, only carnal solutions. Do not go and talk to a brother while you are upset, and do not cleave to another backbiter or gossiper to feed your anger; cleave to somebody positive that is a peacemaker and solution minded.

Give place to the law of the Most High: whatever situation you are going through, the solution is in the Bible, so do not let anger close the book on you.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted of him, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law and the knowledge of his omnipotency.
precepts.point: Everything is in steps, including wisdom; the fear of the Lord is the first step to being accepted of him, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law and the knowledge of his omnipotency.

note.label: Job 28: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found

precepts.why:
Everything is in steps, including wisdom. “The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted of him, and wisdom obtaineth his love. The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.”

“The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.” That is the wisdom Job says cannot be gotten for gold or valued with the gold of Ophir. It is not in the depth or the sea; it is in the fear of the Lord, the first step to being accepted of him, in the performance of the law, and in knowing his omnipotency, that he made us and can take us out.

precepts.text: The doctrine of life is knowing and keeping the commandments of the Most High.
precepts.point: The prophets spoke in similitudes, so not everyone will understand; the Most High shows His secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those He chooses to teach.

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

precepts.why:
“The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.”

The doctrine of life is knowing and keeping the commandments of the Most High. That is the milk the breasts hold, and lying all night betwixt the breasts is meditating on it.

precepts.text: A man is known by his look and countenance, so the sin declares itself.
precepts.point: The show of their countenance witnesses against them, and they declare their sin as Sodom and hide it not. You can know a sodomite when you see him, whatever he wants to call himself, because his whole countenance, the way he walks, acts, and talks, shows it; they are flamboyant.

note.label: Isaiah 3: The Nation Turned Upside Down

precepts.why:
“The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not.” Ecclesiasticus lays it out: “A man may be known by his look, and one that hath understanding by his countenance, when thou meetest him.” A man is known by his look and his countenance, so the sin declares itself.

You can know a sodomite when you see him, whatever he wants to call himself, because his whole countenance, the way he walks, acts and talks, shows it; they are flamboyant. They declare their sin as Sodom and hide it not. “Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.” There is always a payment for sin: “Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen: because their tongue and their doings are against the Lord”.

precepts.text: The Most High took the wife away because such things cause even prophets of understanding to fall away from Him.
precepts.point: Ezekiel spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening his wife died, and he did in the morning as he was commanded. This shows the life of a prophet, whose purpose is above family, love, and children, so when a wife or a distraction interferes with the work the Most High assigned, the purpose comes first.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

precepts.why:
The Most High takes away “the desire of thine eyes with a stroke”, Ezekiel's wife, and tells him not to mourn or weep. Why take the wife? “Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away: and he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent.”

Such things cause even prophets of understanding to fall away from Him. This is the life of a prophet, whose purpose is above family, love and children. Ezekiel spoke to the people in the morning, “and at even my wife died”, and he did in the morning as he was commanded: bound his tire, put on his shoes, covered not his lips and ate not the bread of men.

When a wife or a distraction interferes with the work the Most High assigned, the purpose comes first.

precepts.text: A lack of financial power or status can be the very thing the Most High uses to hinder a man from sinning, because give him the means and he will do the evil.
precepts.point: The Most High is the one who brings a man low. Sometimes he withholds money, status, or a job to hinder a man from sinning, the way he removed King Manasseh from his power. Many hurtful lusts come from the love of money, and celebrities get caught up in wickedness because riches in the hand of a man who has sin become a tool for evil. He wants to teach you discipline and contentment first, so that when the money comes it is only a tool to pay your bills and support the truth, not to live in the delicacies of this life.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“And if for want of power he be hindered from sinning, yet when he findeth opportunity he will do evil.” A lack of financial power or status can be the very thing the Most High uses to hinder a man from sinning. Give him the means and he will do the evil.

Sometimes he withholds money, status or a job for that reason, the way he removed King Manasseh from his power. That is why handing silver and gold to a man whose condition you do not understand is not the help it looks like.

Definitions read in class: exquisite describes something of flawless craftsmanship, delicate beauty, or rare and appealing excellence, of special beauty or charm; subtle describes something delicate, precise, or difficult to perceive, details and changes that are not immediately obvious and require careful thought and close attention to notice. I will add something to the dictionary's list of a face, a flower, coloring, music, or poetry: a doctrine. Many have low self-esteem and low self-worth, and they seek salvation for their enemies while their enemies have them captive. You want heaven for your enemies while you are in their hell?
